title: Post-incident timeline and SLA credit proposal — Dec 12 2026
summary: Draft customer-facing post-incident note that (1) provides a clear minute-by-minute timeline, (2) explains root cause at a customer level, (3) offers an SLA credit calculation and proposed customer outreach cadence, and (4) includes suggested short updates suitable for the public status page. Intended for review by CS leadership and legal before distribution.
incident_overview: On 2026-12-10 between 08:42 and 11:27 UTC, a subset of hosted inference requests experienced elevated error rates and timeouts when routed through the primary US-west region. Impact included failed generation requests for ~14% of requests with long-tail latency increases for an additional ~9%. This affected customers with traffic routed to the affected pool (hosted endpoint tiers: standard and burst). Dedicated and Private deployments were not impacted.
impact: User-facing symptoms: request failures (HTTP 500/502), increased token latency (50–300% above baseline), and several customers reporting degraded application UX during peak windows. Estimated customers impacted: ~120 tenants (primarily mid-market), with ~18 customers showing >2% of daily requests failing during the incident window. No data loss or exfiltration detected.
timeline:
2026-12-10 08:42 UTC — Automated alerts: increased 5xx errors and queuing on inference router
2026-12-10 08:45 UTC — On-call SRE team paged, initial triage started (router + autoscaler checks)
2026-12-10 08:54 UTC — Observed spike in request retries causing queue amplification; temporary mitigation: rate limiting adjustments applied to reduce retry storm
2026-12-10 09:10 UTC — Root cause hypothesis formed: mis-specified kernel fallback selector triggered for a recently onboarded quantized model variant (model: red-model-q4b-v2)
2026-12-10 09:33 UTC — Engine team rolled a targeted config change to disable the new fallback path; partial recovery in error rate observed
2026-12-10 10:05 UTC — Autoscaler oscillation detected due to amplified retries; a safer autoscaling floor applied to stabilize capacity
2026-12-10 10:46 UTC — Error rates returned to baseline for majority of tenants; routing policy adjustments completed to only route to validated model variants
2026-12-10 11:27 UTC — Incident declared resolved for customer-facing services; internal monitoring kept open for 48h for regression detection
root_cause: A kernel-selection change merged as part of a runtime optimization targeted at quantized model variants included an incomplete compatibility check. Under particular sequence-length distributions and request-retry patterns, the fallback kernel path caused thread contention and elevated latencies which cascaded into retries and autoscaler instability. The change passed unit tests but lacked sufficient integration testing for production traffic patterns.
immediate_mitigation_and_workarounds: 1) Disabled the new kernel fallback selector for the affected model variant across the US-west pool. 2) Applied short-term rate-limit thresholds to curb retry amplification. 3) Raised autoscaling minimum to prevent oscillation while stabilizing queues. Workarounds for customers: pin to an older model variant (red-model-fp16-v1) if they rely on low-latency SLAs and temporarily reduce client-side retry aggressiveness.
long_term_remediation:
- Revert-or-redesign the kernel fallback implementation with stricter compatibility checks and expanded integration tests that emulate production retry and sequence-length distributions.
- Add e2e staging traffic replay harnesses that include customer workload shapes.
- Improve canary rollout gating: require low-latency percentile checks and synthetic retry storm tests before enabling new kernel selectors in production.
- Dashboard and alerting improvements: surface sudden retry amplification and autoscaler oscillation as dedicated incident signals.
sla_compensation_proposal: Proposal: Offer impacted customers an SLA credit equal to the proportion of total request failures during the incident window applied to one month of invoice for hosted API usage. Calculation example to include with notice: if a tenant observed 3% of requests failing during the 2h45m window, we propose a 3% credit on that tenant's next monthly hosted API invoice, with a floor of $100 and a cap of $25,000 per tenant. For customers under committed Dedicated contracts, propose a case-by-case credit and an optional operational review call. Request legal review of TOS language before final publication.
proposed_status_page_updates:
Initial (while investigating): 'We are investigating elevated error rates affecting a subset of hosted inference requests in US-west. Engineers are actively triaging; impact limited to hosted API standard tiers.'
Mitigated (after partial fixes): 'We implemented a mitigation to reduce error rates and stabilize routing. Some customers may still experience intermittent failures — we continue monitoring.'
Resolved (after stabilization): 'Service has returned to expected levels for hosted API in US-west. We will publish a customer-facing postmortem within 72 hours.'
Postmortem published: 'A postmortem describing root cause, customer impact, and remediation steps is now available. Affected customers will receive SLA credit proposals and optional follow-up calls.'
recommended_customer_actions:
- If you experienced persistent failures, collect request IDs and times and provide them to support for expedited reconciliation.
- Reduce aggressive client-side retry backoff (suggest initial backoff >= 200ms and exponential cap) while we complete rollout gates.
- Consider pinning to red-model-fp16-v1 for low-latency critical paths until the redesigned fallback is validated.
Support will provide a targeted script to identify impacted requests per tenant.
communication_notes_for_account_teams: Suggested email subject: 'Redwood: Update & proposed SLA credit for Dec 10 incident affecting hosted API (US-west)'. Body bullets: one-sentence summary, customer-specific impact (we will fill using support logs), proposed credit amount and calculation link, offer of operational review call, and timeline for final postmortem. Attach FAQ and short status page snippets. For enterprise accounts, escalate to solutions engineering to offer a dedicated operational review within 72 hours.
